September 28, 2026

US intelligence says Chinese groups are aiding Iranian targeting of American forces

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @groundnews

US intelligence assessments described to CNN by four sources say Chinese groups have provided Iran with satellite imagery and intelligence that improved its targeting of US military bases in the Middle East and of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Officials believe the imagery gave Iran precision it could not have achieved alone in a July strike on a US base in Jordan that killed three American service members, and has helped time drone launches at ships. A US official disputed that outside help has changed Iranian capabilities, while Ambassador to China David Perdue said Trump told Xi Jinping that any assistance to Iran, direct or indirect, is unacceptable. In May the State Department sanctioned three Chinese satellite companies over imagery used in Iranian strikes.

Eight Marines injured in undisclosed Iranian missile strike in Strait of Hormuz

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

An Iranian anti-ship cruise missile struck a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz on September 14, injuring eight US Marines, according to three US officials cited by NBC News. The Marines suffered smoke inhalation and possible concussion or traumatic brain injury symptoms, and all have returned to duty. The vessel was not a US Navy ship, and the attack was not publicly disclosed at the time.

US ambassador says Trump offered to sell American weapons to China

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

US Ambassador to China David Perdue told Fox News that Trump asked Xi Jinping during the Chinese president's state visit to Washington whether he would like to buy American weapons. Such a sale would break US law, and the State Department said no offer or plan exists. The remark came during a discussion of arms sales to Taiwan, where a $14 billion package has awaited Trump's sign-off since December; he previously described the package as a negotiating chip in dealings with Beijing.

US reported to be laying groundwork for an invasion of Cuba

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

CBS reporting indicates the United States is making assessments and preparing the groundwork for a possible invasion of Cuba. No timeline or scope for such an operation was given.

Education Department rule will cut student loans for lower-earning majors

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

The Department of Education has finalised a rule that will bar federal student loan access for degree programs whose graduates do not earn enough, taking effect in 2027. Affected fields include social work, art, religious studies, teaching aide and music programs, and cosmetic certification programs. The department plans to use IRS data to compare graduates' salaries four years out against those of people the same age holding only a high school diploma.

New York prosecutors reopen criminal investigation into seven Cornell fraternity members

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

New York prosecutors have reopened a criminal investigation into seven Chi Psi fraternity members at Cornell University and will present evidence to a grand jury in central New York, which will decide whether to indict. The move follows a lawsuit filed two weeks ago by a Jane Doe student alleging she was drugged and gang-raped, and alleging the university responded with minimal discipline such as essay assignments. Prosecutors had initially declined to bring charges. Commentary has pushed back on the "Cornell 7" label, arguing the men should be identified individually and face expulsion and trial.

Texas Republican candidate Bo French called for Obama's execution in deleted posts

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A CNN investigation has surfaced deleted posts by Bo French, a Republican candidate for statewide office in Texas, calling for the public execution of former President Barack Obama. In one post French wrote that the penalty for treason used to be death, even for a former president, and used the hashtag "hang him high" in reference to Obama and Representative Adam Schiff. Greg Abbott, Ken Paxton and the state Republican Party have not commented. French has previously drawn attention for remarks directed at University of Texas at Austin students.

White House deputy chief of staff's AI celebration video draws bipartisan backlash

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

White House Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino posted an AI-generated video depicting administration figures celebrating with champagne as ultra-wealthy elites. The post drew criticism from Democrats and from Republicans and White House allies, who said it reads as a celebration while Americans struggle with costs. The reaction has been framed as a "let them eat cake" moment for the administration.

Republican senators break with Trump as midterms approach

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Five Republicans now back some form of investigation into Donald Trump Jr.'s ties to a Russian oligarch who helped pay for part of his wedding. Senator John Kennedy said Trump's name should not go on buildings and that taxpayer money should not fund Trump campaign advertising, while some Republicans have removed Trump from their websites. Trump has said he rejected a ceasefire with Iran despite an Iranian offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, leaving little prospect of falling gas prices before November.

Marjorie Taylor Greene questions timing of reported migrant caravan

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene responded to a post claiming more than 400 migrants, predominantly from Honduras, entered Mexico bound for the US southern border by questioning why a caravan is appearing now. She said no caravan has headed to the border in several years and suggested the GOP needs to frighten voters ahead of the coming election. The claim that the group is heading to the US border is not fully verified.

Utah data center buildout advances without environmental review

tags: tech, climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Utah now has the third-largest data center pipeline in the country by power demand, behind only Texas and Virginia, with most projects sited in rural counties such as Delta and Box Elder. The largest, Kevin O'Leary's Stratos project near the Great Salt Lake, would consume more than twice the electricity the entire state uses today and was approved by the Military Installation Development Authority, an unelected state board chaired by the Senate president, with no environmental review or public comment period. Residents who sought to put the project on the ballot were rejected by the county attorney, a decision now being litigated, and under MIDA rules a county's consent cannot be withdrawn. Concerns raised include PFAS used in cooling and fire suppression entering water supplies in the nation's second-driest state.

Blue Cross Blue Shield says AI documentation is driving up hospital billing

tags: health, tech, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

The Blue Cross Blue Shield Association says insurers are paying out nearly a billion dollars more than usual because hospitals are using AI-assisted documentation to identify additional diagnoses that raise reimbursement rates, without corresponding increases in the care delivered. Insurers themselves are also deploying AI, in their case to deny claims, in well-documented cases. The combined effect falls on patients through denied claims and higher premiums.

Atlanta man jailed 30 days sues city over case built with Flock surveillance data

tags: surveillance, legal, privacy
sources: @aaronparnas

Davis McNair, an Army veteran and doctoral student in Atlanta, was arrested in 2024 in connection with a road rage shooting and spent 30 days in the Fulton County Jail before the case was dismissed with prejudice. Investigative records reported by Atlanta's 11Alive show surveillance camera technology was used to identify vehicles that became part of the case against him. He has filed a federal civil rights lawsuit against the city of Atlanta, and his legal team is weighing whether to add Flock Safety as a defendant.

California declares emergency over Kelvin wave expected to raise sea levels

tags: climate
sources: @aaronparnas

Governor Gavin Newsom has declared a state of emergency as California braces for a planetary-scale Kelvin wave that could raise sea levels along the coast by up to a foot over the coming months. The wave, fuelled by the current strong El Niño in the Pacific, carries warm water thousands of miles from the western Pacific along the equator toward the US West Coast. Officials are concerned about coastal damage and erosion in Southern California and elsewhere in the state.

UN warns global water cycle is becoming more erratic as reserves decline

tags: climate
sources: @groundnews

The World Meteorological Organization said droughts and floods are increasing as freshwater reserves fall, with global rivers recording one of their three driest years in 35 years during 2025. Glaciers lost about 1,400 gigatonnes of water between 2023 and 2025, and nearly two-thirds of monitored groundwater wells were outside historical norms. Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said, "We are spending our reserves." The agency warned a strengthening El Niño, expected to be the strongest in four decades of comparable records, could deepen drought in some regions while raising flood risk in others.

Abbas sets first Palestinian legislative elections in 20 years for November 28

tags: politics, war
sources: @groundnews

Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas announced legislative elections for November 28, the first such vote in two decades, as his government faces international pressure to enact governance reforms. Fatah officials cite unresolved disputes among Palestinian factions and Israeli restrictions on election materials entering Gaza as obstacles, while Hamas says it plans to take part and is discussing a coalition to challenge Fatah. Speaking to the UN General Assembly by video after the United States denied him a visa, Abbas said his reform program was complete and urged Washington to restore dialogue. He has also pledged a presidential election in 2027.

Trump floats replacing White House press room with a gold swimming pool

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The president has suggested removing the James S. Brady press briefing room and rebuilding the FDR swimming pool beneath it with gold leaf and gold trim. The pool, built in 1933, sits under the briefing room and currently holds no water. The briefing room is the main venue through which the administration communicates with the public.

Christian nationalist pastors argue for rolling back women's rights

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Podcast remarks by two white Christian nationalist pastors argued that women having unsupervised access to one another, holding political office, and living unattached to a husband or father have made women anxious and miserable. Among the figures cited is Doug Wilson, described as the personal pastor of Pete Hegseth, who has called for repealing women's right to vote in favour of one vote per household. The remarks were contrasted with the rapid loss of Afghan women's rights after the Taliban seized Kabul in August 2021, including bans on high school in September 2021, travel without a chaperone in December 2021, mandatory face coverings in May 2022, university attendance and NGO work in December 2022, beauty salons in July 2023, and a 2024 morality law restricting women's voices in public.

Grand Staircase-Escalante faces funding and boundary cuts at 30

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument marked its 30th anniversary after the administration cut its boundaries this summer, saying the monument was too large for BLM staff and budget to manage. Local business owners say the management budget has been reduced to roughly $1.6 million, leaving the monument without rangers, maintained trails or trash collection. In Boulder, Utah, a town of about 250 people, Hell's Backbone Grill has become one of the county's largest employers on the strength of visitors drawn by the monument. Polling cited indicates seven in ten Utah voters oppose cuts to public lands agencies and two in three want the monuments restored.

E. coli outbreak tied to raw milk cheese prompts multistate recall

tags: health
sources: @groundnews

Sierra Nevada Cheese Company has recalled four Graziers grass-fed raw milk cheeses — medium cheddar, sharp cheddar, jalapeño jack and Monterey jack — linked to a multistate E. coli outbreak that has hospitalised at least eight people, according to the FDA. Federal health officials had identified 13 cases nationwide as of Friday and are investigating the source and whether other products are affected. The FDA told consumers not to eat, serve or sell the cheese and to check refrigerators and freezers given its long shelf life.

GAO finds Cannon Air Force Base personnel travel up to 350 miles for medical care

tags: defence, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

A Government Accountability Office report found service members at Cannon Air Force Base travelled as far as 350 miles each way to obtain medical care. The travel consumed at least 5,000 duty days in fiscal year 2025.

Trump heckled at President's Cup over Epstein files

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

While giving a speech at the President's Cup at his own golf course, Trump was heckled and called a profanity-laced accusation of pedophilia, which reporters confirmed. The heckling was tied to continuing public pressure over the release of the remaining Jeffrey Epstein files and accountability for survivors.
